d1478b463999e146e17f61b5af99e9aca1549390.summary: SentinelOne's report ties the Hafnium group (also called Silk Typhoon) to Chinese contractor firms. It says DOJ indictments named hackers Xu Zewei and Zhang Yu, who worked under the Shanghai State Security Bureau, and Yin Kecheng and Zhou Shuai. It identifies 10+ patents held by Shanghai Firetech for intrusive forensics and data collection tools, including Apple device capabilities, and says these tools may exceed those publicly attributed to Hafnium. It also covers the 2021 Exchange Server exploitation that followed ProxyLogon, and China's response to the 2021 joint statement. The report…

hedges: It remains unclear how exactly the exploit proliferated ahead of the patch.
The exact date Hafnium's campaign began is unclear.
Yin Kecheng likely worked alongside Xu and Zhang, though in what capacity is unclear.
It is unknown what of Yin's work, access, or tooling Zhou was trying to push.
It is possible that none of the tooling uncovered by this report was ever deployed in offensive operations.
There is good reason to believe only some of Shanghai Firetech's activities have been uncovered or made public.
Shanghai Firetech likely offers offensive services to additional customers beyond Shanghai; no public tenders or contracts were found.
It is unclear whether the absence of Chongqing Firetech from the indictment indicates it was not involved in Hafnium-cluster activity.
